name: Hobart
tagline: Tasmania's harbour capital, where colonial sandstone meets a mountain and a famously eccentric art museum.
description: Hobart is the capital of Tasmania and Australia's second oldest city, set along the Derwent River beneath Kunanyi / Mount Wellington. It began as a penal colony, and colonial sandstone warehouses and historic buildings still stand around Salamanca Place and Battery Point. Visitors come for the museums, the food and the waterfront. The Sydney to Hobart Yacht Race finishes at Constitution Dock in Sullivans Cove.
whyVisitSubjects: the Museum of Old and New Art on the Derwent at Berriedale, ideally the ferry arriving at its jetty
the view from Kunanyi / Mount Wellington's summit over Hobart and the Derwent
the row of sandstone warehouses on Salamanca Place
a Tasmanian devil or other native animal at Bonorong Wildlife Sanctuary

goodToKnow.title: Book MONA ahead
goodToKnow.detail: MONA is open Thursday to Monday and recommends booking ahead, as timed entry slots are limited; ferries leave from Brooke Street Pier.

goodToKnow.title: Pack for the summit
goodToKnow.detail: Hobart is mild, but the top of Kunanyi / Mount Wellington is typically 10 degrees or more colder than the city, and in snow the road can be congested or closed, so check conditions before you go.

goodToKnow.title: Walk the waterfront
goodToKnow.detail: Sullivans Cove, Salamanca Place and Battery Point are all within walking distance of each other, so you can leave the car behind for a day in the centre.

bestTimeBlurb: Hobart is most pleasant in {months}, when days are mild and long, with summer highs averaging around 21 °C. Winter is cold, and snow often caps the mountain above the city.

name: Huon Valley
tagline: Orchards, tall forest and alpine plateaus along Australia's southernmost road.
description: The Huon Valley runs south of Hobart along the Huon River and the D'Entrecasteaux Channel, and is home to Australia's southernmost inhabited settlements. Orchards produce roughly a tenth of the country's apples, alongside pears and cherries, and the valley's towns are scattered along the Huon Highway. Beyond the farmland lie tall-forest reserves, dolomite caves and the glacial country of Hartz Mountains National Park. Expect cool weather even in summer, with frosts common between April and October.
whyVisit: Hike to Hartz Mountains' glacial lakes
whyVisitSubjects: the Tahune AirWalk elevated walkway among forest canopy above the Huon River
a glacial tarn such as Lake Esperance in Hartz Mountains National Park
decorated chambers inside Newdegate Cave at Hastings Caves

goodToKnow.title: Parks pass for Hartz
goodToKnow.detail: Hartz Mountains National Park needs a valid Tasmanian parks pass; buy one online or at a visitor centre. Hastings Caves needs no pass, but cave tours are guided, run hourly and are ticketed at the visitor centre, where you check in 45 minutes before.

goodToKnow.title: Cold, even in summer
goodToKnow.detail: The valley rarely tops 20 °C and the mountains are colder still, with snow possible in the cooler months; carry a warm jacket and rain layer on any walk.

goodToKnow.title: Plan for distances
goodToKnow.detail: Towns are strung along the Huon Highway and the far-south attractions are long drives from Huonville, so allow a full day for Tahune or Hastings.

bestTimeBlurb: The warmest weather for walking and driving is {months}. The high country can be snowy in the cooler months, and the Hartz Mountains road can close in winter snow.

name: Bruny Island
tagline: A car-ferry island of a lighthouse, long beaches and white wallabies south of Hobart.
description: Bruny Island lies off Tasmania's south-east coast and is made up of North and South Bruny, joined by a narrow isthmus called the Neck. North Bruny is mostly flat farmland, while South Bruny is hillier and more forested, with sections of South Bruny National Park. Visitors come for the coastal walks, the lighthouse, boat cruises from Adventure Bay and wildlife, including white wallabies and a little penguin colony at the Neck. It is a day trip from Hobart but has accommodation for longer stays.
whyVisitSubjects: the view from The Hummock lookout across the Neck isthmus on Bruny Island
Cape Bruny Lighthouse on its headland
the sea cliffs of Fluted Cape in South Bruny National Park

goodToKnow.title: Car ferry from Kettering
goodToKnow.detail: A car ferry crosses from Kettering to Roberts Bay and vehicles pay a fare; foot passengers travel free, but there is no public transport at either end.

goodToKnow.title: Bring your own car
goodToKnow.detail: There is no car hire on the island, and some hire companies bar their cars from the ferry or do not insure them on it, so check before you book.

goodToKnow.title: Parks pass for South Bruny
goodToKnow.detail: South Bruny National Park, including Cape Bruny Lighthouse and its walks, requires a valid Tasmanian parks pass. Allow time: the drive from the ferry to Adventure Bay takes about 45 minutes, and the lighthouse is another half hour on.

bestTimeBlurb: Calm, mild days for the ferry, cruises and walks are most likely in {months}.

name: Mount Field National Park
tagline: A park for all seasons, from tree-fern forest to snow-dusted alpine tarns.
description: Mount Field is one of Tasmania's oldest national parks and rises from tall swamp-gum and tree-fern forest to snow-gum country and alpine moorland. The lower section around the visitor centre has short, easy walks, while the road to Lake Dobson climbs through rainforest to glacial lakes and longer day walks. In winter the high ground is dusted with snow and used for cross-country skiing, and in autumn the Tarn Shelf slopes turn colour.
whyVisit: Hike the Tarn Shelf alpine lakes
See autumn colour on the high plateau
whyVisitSubjects: Russell Falls, the tiered cascade in tree-fern forest
tarns and alpine moorland on the Tarn Shelf
autumn-coloured vegetation on the Tarn Shelf above Lake Dobson

goodToKnow.title: Parks pass required
goodToKnow.detail: A valid Tasmanian parks pass is required for entry; buy one online or at the visitor centre at the park entrance.

goodToKnow.title: Alpine weather
goodToKnow.detail: The Lake Dobson road climbs to the high country, where conditions are much colder than the visitor centre and snow can close or restrict the road in winter.

goodToKnow.title: Two sections, two kinds of walk
goodToKnow.detail: The Russell Falls area suits short, easy walks, while Lake Dobson is the start for long day walks such as the Tarn Shelf, so choose by your time and fitness.

bestTimeBlurb: Summer and early autumn, {months}, are best for the high-country walks, with autumn colour on the Tarn Shelf in the cooler end of that range. Winter brings snow and cross-country skiing to the upper park.

name: Southwest National Park
tagline: Tasmania's largest national park: a remote lake, a hydro dam and a wilderness coastline.
description: Southwest National Park is Tasmania's largest park and part of the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area. The Gordon River Road runs west from Maydena to Lake Pedder, Lake Gordon and the Gordon Dam at Strathgordon, while walkers tackle the long tracks beyond the roads. The wilder parts of the park, including the south coast, are reached on foot, by boat or by air, and conditions change quickly.
whyVisit: See Lake Pedder from its shore
whyVisitSubjects: the curved concrete wall of the Gordon Dam and the gorge below
Lake Pedder with surrounding mountains
the wild beaches and coastline of the South Coast Track

goodToKnow.title: Parks pass needed
goodToKnow.detail: A valid Tasmanian parks pass is required to enter the park.

goodToKnow.title: Register overnight walks
goodToKnow.detail: Overnight walker registration is required for some walks, including the Western Arthur Range and Mount Anne Circuit; be prepared for extreme, rapidly changing weather.

goodToKnow.title: Check access notices
goodToKnow.detail: From 1 September 2026 West Picton Road is closed at Cook Creek, so the Eastern Arthur Range Traverse and Mount Picton Track need an extra walk from the closure. Check current notices before you go.

bestTimeBlurb: Summer is the most reliable season for the road lookouts and multi-day walks, and {months} give the longest days. Rain, wind and cold are possible in any month.

name: Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park
tagline: Rainforest rivers and quartzite peaks beside the Lyell Highway.
description: Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park protects a wild river system and the white quartzite summit of Frenchmans Cap in the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area. Short walks from the Lyell Highway lead to waterfalls and lookouts, while the Frenchmans Cap Track is a multi-day hike. The Franklin River itself is a remote, challenging trip for experienced paddlers or guided parties.
whyVisitSubjects: Nelson Falls on the Nelson River
the view over the Franklin River valley from Donaghys Hill Lookout
the white quartzite summit of Frenchmans Cap

goodToKnow.title: Parks pass needed
goodToKnow.detail: A valid Tasmanian parks pass is required for entry to the park.

goodToKnow.title: Wet, changeable weather
goodToKnow.detail: This is the wettest part of Tasmania, with more than 1900 mm of rain a year, so carry waterproofs for even the short Lyell Highway walks, and treat the Frenchmans Cap Track as a hard, weather-exposed 3-5 day trip.

goodToKnow.title: Rafting is guided
goodToKnow.detail: The Franklin River is a multi-day wilderness trip for experienced paddlers or guided parties; book a guided expedition rather than turning up at the roadside.

bestTimeBlurb: Summer, {months}, gives the best odds of clear weather for the lookouts, Frenchmans Cap and rafting. Rain and cold are possible at any time of year.

name: West Coast Tasmania
tagline: Remote harbour, convict ruins and mining country around Strahan and Queenstown.
description: Tasmania's west coast is one of the most isolated parts of Australia, about 300 km west of Hobart. Strahan, a port town on Macquarie Harbour, is the base for Gordon River cruises and the convict ruins of Sarah Island, while Queenstown and Zeehan keep the story of the region's copper and silver mining. Ocean Beach, a huge surf beach of dunes and Southern Ocean swell, lies nearby, and the West Coast Wilderness Railway runs from Strahan's Regatta Point.
whyVisitSubjects: a Macquarie Harbour cruise on the Gordon River in rainforest
the ruins of the convict penal station on Sarah Island
the Iron Blow mine pit above Queenstown

goodToKnow.title: Book cruises ahead
goodToKnow.detail: Gordon River and Sarah Island visits depart from Strahan by cruise, so reserve in advance through the visitor centre or the operator.

goodToKnow.title: Take care at Ocean Beach
goodToKnow.detail: Ocean Beach is a 40 km beach of large dunes where waves arrive from as far as Patagonia; take care near the surf.

goodToKnow.title: Long distances
goodToKnow.detail: The coast is about 300 km from Hobart, with Queenstown, Zeehan and Strahan spread across the region, so allow at least a night rather than a day trip.

bestTimeBlurb: Summer, {months}, is the most reliable season for the cruises and viewpoints, though the west coast is wet and windy in any month. Winter can be cold and stormy.
